messages.content: Write a polished 400-to-500-word contemporary American English scene with three adult friends preparing a simple meal together. Give each person a distinct voice and level of involvement. Let conversation overlap, let someone be distracted, and let a small disagreement happen without becoming dramatic. Include practical action and a quiet emotional beat. Keep the prose grounded and avoid making every line funny.

“Who bought cilantro?”

Sam looked up from the cutting board.

“I did.”

“Why?” Riley asked.

“Because the recipe said cilantro.”

Casey opened the refrigerator. “We have cilantro.”

Riley pointed at the bag. “We don't need cilantro.”

Sam stared at her. “You told me to get everything on the list.”

“I wrote down limes.”

“You wrote down cilantro.”

“I did not.”

Casey shut the refrigerator.

“You did.”

Riley looked at her.

“Whose side are you on?”

“The side with the evidence.”

Sam smiled.

Riley reached for the phone on the counter.

“Where's the list?”

“Right there.”

She picked it up.

A moment later, she frowned.

“You're right.”

Sam raised both hands.

“I would like that noted for the record.”

“Don't get carried away.”

Casey started heating a pan.

“You two argue about groceries like you're negotiating a merger.”

“It matters,” Riley said.

“It really doesn't.”

Sam added oil to the pan.

“What are you doing?” Riley asked.

“Cooking.”

“You're supposed to wait.”

“For what?”

“The pan.”

“The pan is hot.”

“It's not hot enough.”

Sam checked it.

“It feels hot.”

“You are not a thermometer.”

Casey laughed.

Sam looked at her. “You're not helping.”

“I know.”

The kitchen filled with the smell of garlic when Casey dropped it into the pan.

Riley leaned against the counter and watched for a second.

“Do you ever just let somebody else do things?” Sam asked.

“No.”

“Why?”

Riley shrugged.

“Someone has to notice when we're doing it wrong.”

Casey looked over.

“That's a terrible answer.”

Riley smiled, but only for a second.

The phone on the counter buzzed.

She glanced at the screen and went still.

Sam noticed first.

“Everything okay?”

“Yeah.”

Riley put the phone facedown.

Casey turned the stove lower.

“Want me to?”

Riley shook her head.

“No.”

“Okay.”

Sam started chopping again.

Nobody asked a second time.

After a minute, Riley picked up the cilantro.

“Hand me that bowl.”

Sam passed it over.

She started tearing the leaves by hand.

Casey tasted the sauce.

“Needs salt.”

Riley handed her the bowl.

“Fix it.”

Casey nodded.

Sam smiled. “Look at us.”

Riley glanced at him.

“What?”

“We're functioning.”

“Don't ruin it.”
